transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Um, yeah... so I guess the main thing that pushed me to finally come in is work. I process insurance claims, and I just keep getting up from my workstation during the day. Like, constantly. Even when I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish my claim reviews, I just can't stay in my chair. 

I'll get up to get water, or... well, our office just got one of those fancy espresso machines in the breakroom. It's actually really nice, it grinds the beans right there and everything. I used to work at a coffee shop back when I was taking some classes at the community college, so I'm kind of a snob about it, you know? Most office coffee is basically dirt, but this one is actually decent. I tried to show my coworker Greg how to use the steam wand yesterday because he kept burning the milk. 

But anyway, yeah, my supervisor is starting to get pretty annoyed because I'm just never at my desk doing my batches when I'm supposed to be.
Has this kind of restlessness and trouble staying seated been something you've dealt with since you were a kid, or is this a newer change for you?

I mean, looking back, it’s definitely not a brand new thing for me. I don't know if I was always getting out of my chair as much back then, but in elementary school, my teachers used to always write notes to my parents saying I was a bright kid, but I constantly lost my worksheets. 

I remember this one time I lost my math packet and my teacher made me clean out my whole desk to find it, and it was just full of random stuff. Like, I had this huge collection of those Crazy Bones toys—do you remember those? They were these little plastic guys you'd flick at each other. I had the rare glow-in-the-dark ones, and I'd just play with them inside my desk where the teacher couldn't see. The school actually ended up banning them completely because kids were getting into arguments over trades at recess. My friend Josh got sent to the principal's office for throwing one at a kid's head, which was pretty wild. 

But um, what was I... oh, right. Yeah, so my teachers were always writing that I missed instructions and needed constant reminders to actually finish my classwork. So I guess I've always kind of struggled with staying on track.
Outside of work, do you notice this same restlessness or trouble focusing—like at home, when driving, or during other activities?

Um, outside of work... yeah, I mean, I guess I don't really notice the getting up from my chair thing as much at home. But I definitely have trouble focusing on stuff. Like, I'll sit down to watch a movie, and I just can't make it through without pulling out my phone. 

I was trying to watch that new sci-fi movie on Netflix the other night, the one with the huge spaceship that looks like a giant donut? The special effects were actually pretty crazy. I was reading this article about how they did the CGI for it, and apparently, they used the same rendering software that they used for those old Lord of the Rings movies. Which is wild, right? Because those movies came out, like, twenty years ago, and they still look better than half the stuff coming out now. I actually went to New Zealand a few years ago and did the whole Hobbiton tour. It was super cool, but it rained the whole time, so my shoes were just completely ruined by the end of it. I had these really nice boots, too, the kind that are supposed to be waterproof, but they definitely weren't.

But, uh, what were we talking about? Oh, right, at home. Yeah, I don't know, I just... I don't really notice the restlessness as much there, I guess? Or maybe I just don't pay attention to it.
Do you often find yourself talking excessively, interrupting others, or blurting out answers before someone finishes speaking?

Um... I don't think so? I mean, I don't really notice myself talking too much, or at least nobody's ever complained about it to my face. My sister talks a lot, though. Like, she can just go on and on for hours without taking a breath. She actually just started this new podcast about true crime, which I guess makes sense because she's always been obsessed with that stuff. 

She was telling me about this one case from the 70s where this guy just vanished from a locked room, and they never found him. They think he might have crawled through the air vents, but the vents were only, like, eight inches wide. I don't know how anyone could fit in there. I get claustrophobic just thinking about it. When I was a kid, I got stuck in one of those plastic tube slides at McDonald's, and the fire department actually had to come get me out. It was so embarrassing. 

But, uh, no, I don't really think I interrupt people or blurt things out. At least, not that I've noticed.

Aside from getting up at your desk, do you often feel physically restless or fidgety—like tapping your foot, fidgeting with your hands, or feeling like you can't relax—even when you're sitting somewhere else, like at home or in a meeting?

Um, yeah, I definitely do that. Like, whenever we have those long team meetings or, you know, those mandatory training sessions at work, I'm usually bouncing my leg the whole time. Or I'll be clicking my pen over and over, just shifting around in my chair constantly, even when I'm really trying hard to look like I'm focused on the presentation. 

Actually, speaking of pens, I just bought this really nice fountain pen online a couple weeks ago. I thought getting a fancy pen would make me want to take better notes during our claims reviews. It was one of those expensive German ones with the gold nib. But I ended up dropping it on the kitchen floor the second day I had it, and the tip got completely bent backward. I tried to fix it with some needle-nose pliers, but I just ended up scratching it and making it worse. My grandpa actually used to collect vintage pens. He had this huge wooden display case in his den that he built entirely by himself. He was really good at woodworking. He made me a birdhouse once when I was little, but a squirrel ended up chewing through the entrance hole to get to the seeds and completely destroyed the roof. Squirrels are actually crazy destructive, I had no idea. 

But, um... sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling restless. Yeah, I'm definitely always bouncing my leg or messing with my hands when I'm stuck in a meeting.
Do you often have trouble waiting your turn—like in line or in traffic—or find yourself making quick decisions or purchases without really thinking them through first?

Um, not really? Like, waiting in line or sitting in traffic doesn't really bother me that much. I actually kind of like traffic sometimes because it gives me an excuse to just sit and listen to my audiobooks. I've been getting really into historical non-fiction lately. I just finished this huge one about the history of the postal service, which sounds super boring, I know, but it was actually fascinating. Like, back in the early 1900s, people used to literally mail their children through the parcel post. They'd put stamps on their coats and just hand them to the mail carrier because it was cheaper than buying a train ticket. 

Can you imagine doing that now? The liability alone would be insane. Working in insurance, I see some pretty weird policy claims, but if someone tried to file a claim for a lost kid in the mail today, our whole department would probably have a complete meltdown. My supervisor gets stressed out just when someone submits a claim for a water-damaged laptop. He turns bright red and starts sweating through his shirt. It's kind of hard to watch, honestly. I keep telling him he needs to drink less coffee, but he just bought one of those expensive espresso machines for his desk. 

But, uh... yeah. Wait, what were you asking? Oh, waiting my turn and stuff. No, I don't really have a problem with that. And I don't really buy things without thinking about it first, either. I'm usually pretty careful with my money.
Thinking back to when you were a kid, do you remember feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble staying seated in class the way you do now at work?

Um, not really? Like, I wasn't really the kid who was bouncing off the walls or running around the classroom or anything like that. I didn't really get in trouble for getting out of my seat. But... I mean, looking back, the problems I have now aren't really brand new. Like, in elementary school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but I was always losing my worksheets. Like, constantly. I actually remember having this one folder that was supposed to be for homework, and it was just this chaotic mess of crinkled papers. I think I spilled juice on it once and it got all sticky, but I just kept using it anyway. 

My mom tried to get me one of those Trapper Keepers with the velcro flap to help me stay organized. It had this really cool dinosaur on the front—like a T-Rex with lasers coming out of its eyes, which was super popular back then. I loved that thing. But the velcro stopped sticking after a couple of months because it got full of lint and dog hair. We had this Golden Retriever named Buster who shed everywhere. You could just pet him and a whole cloud of fur would come off. He was the best dog, though. He used to try to catch bees in the backyard, and one time he actually got stung on the nose and his whole face swelled up. He looked like a cartoon character. We had to take him to the emergency vet, and it cost my parents a fortune. 

Wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, school. Yeah, I wasn't physically restless, but my teachers always said I missed instructions and they constantly had to remind me to actually finish my classwork. So, yeah, I guess I've always kind of struggled with that kind of stuff.

Did these attention issues—like losing worksheets, missing instructions, or needing constant reminders—cause noticeable problems for you before you turned 12, like affecting your grades or getting you in trouble with teachers?

Um, I don't think so? Like, I don't remember failing classes or getting sent to the principal's office or anything. My grades were usually fine, mostly because my mom was pretty strict and would make me sit at the kitchen counter every afternoon until my homework was done. She'd physically go through my backpack every single day to find whatever I had crumpled up at the bottom. 

We had this really tall kitchen counter with these wooden barstools that would always squeak super loud when you spun them. I used to spin on them constantly until my dad threatened to throw them out. He was always trying to throw out perfectly good furniture, honestly. He actually got really into minimalism for a while after watching some documentary on Netflix. He tried to convince my mom to get rid of the TV and just read books by candlelight, which lasted exactly one night because they tried to read a mystery novel together and my dad knocked over a candle and almost set the living room curtains on fire. The fire department actually had to come, and the fire truck completely blocked our neighbor's driveway. Our neighbor was this older guy who collected vintage cars, and he was so incredibly mad because he was trying to take his pristine '67 Mustang out to a car show that evening. He wouldn't talk to my dad for like six months after that. 

But, uh... wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. What was the question? Oh, right, getting in trouble before I was 12. No, I don't think it really caused any major problems like bad grades or anything, mostly just the teachers being annoyed and having to remind me to pay attention.
Do you often feel like you're 'on the go' or driven by a motor, or have a hard time relaxing and enjoying quiet, low-key activities like reading or sitting quietly?

Um, no? Not really. Like, I don't feel like I'm driven by a motor or anything. I actually really like relaxing and quiet activities. Like I said, I listen to audiobooks a lot, and I also play video games sometimes to unwind. I've been playing this one game where you basically just build a farm and talk to the townspeople. It's super chill. You can plant all these different crops depending on the season, and right now I'm trying to grow a giant pumpkin. You have to arrange the seeds in a specific pattern and water them every single day, and there's a chance they'll merge into one massive pumpkin. 

My friend Sarah actually plays it too, and she got the giant pumpkin on her first try, which is honestly so unfair. She's always been incredibly lucky like that. We went to a carnival once back in college, and she won this giant stuffed bear on the ring toss game. You know how those games are completely rigged, right? Like, the rings are barely bigger than the bottlenecks. But she just tossed it without even aiming and it landed perfectly. She couldn't even fit the bear in her car, so she had to strap it to the roof. We drove all the way back to our dorm with this massive purple bear just staring down at everyone on the highway. We kept getting weird looks from people in minivans. 

But, um... yeah, sorry. What were you asking? Oh, feeling 'on the go' or having a hard time relaxing. No, I don't really have a problem with that. I'm usually pretty happy just sitting around.
